record.paper_title: FPT Suspects and Tough Customers: Open Problems of Downey and Fellows
record.original_question: Given two collections of k multivariate polynomials p1, ..., pk and q1, ..., qk, each represented by listing the monomials with nonzero coefficients, is there a deterministic fixed-parameter algorithm in k for deciding whether the polynomial identity product_{i=1}^k p_i = product_{i=1}^k q_i holds?

evidence.quote: Question: Does the following identity hold?
It could still be a nontrivial question if the problem is in deterministic FPT.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k\ge 1$ be a positive integer regarded as a parameter. The input consists of two lists of $k$ multivariate polynomials over $\mathbb{Z}$ (or $\mathbb{Q}$),
$$p_1,\dots,p_k \quad\text{and}\quad q_1,\dots,q_k,$$
where each polynomial is given explicitly as a sparse representation: a finite list of (monomial, coefficient) pairs containing exactly the monomials with nonzero coefficients. The size of the input is the total bit-length of this representation.

Decide whether the polynomial identity
$$\prod_{i=1}^{k} p_i \;=\; \prod_{i=1}^{k} q_i$$
holds in the polynomial ring.

Question: Does there exist a deterministic fixed-parameter tractable algorithm, with parameter $k$, that solves this decision problem? Equivalently, is there a deterministic algorithm running in time $f(k)\cdot N^{O(1)}$, where $N$ is the input size and $f$ is some computable function, that correctly decides the identity for all inputs?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not turn up a deterministic fixed-parameter algorithm (parameterized by k) for testing the equality of two products of k sparsely represented multivariate polynomials, nor a proof of intractability. Polynomial identity testing in general remains a major open problem regarding deterministic algorithms, and no resolution of this specific parameterized variant could be verified.

status_evidence.title: Equivalence of Polynomial Identity Testing and Deterministic Polynomial Factorization
status_evidence.snippet: Deterministic algorithms for polynomial identity testing and for polynomial factorization are essentially equivalent; both remain major open problems.
status_evidence.claim: Deterministic PIT in general is still open, suggesting the parameterized variant has not been settled affirmatively.

status_evidence.title: A Parameterized Complexity Tutorial - Rod Downey
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of FPT problems and open questions in parameterized complexity by Downey.
status_evidence.claim: No mention of a resolution to the deterministic FPT polynomial product identity question.
